meta.description: Public section registry, the single source of truth for the homepage cards, Find Your Section and section pages. Public fields only: no exact venues, capacities, member or leader data. Edit here to change meeting patterns or section content, then redeploy.

Beavers.intro: Beavers is where the adventure begins. Our youngest members make friends, play games, try new things and get their first taste of the outdoors, all in a safe, welcoming and fun environment.

details.Uniform: Beavers wear a turquoise sweatshirt and a Group scarf (necker). No uniform is needed for the first few sessions, so there's no rush. We can point you to new and second-hand options.
details.Costs: Subscriptions are typically £3 to 5 per week, covering weekly meetings, activities and insurance. Camps and special events cost extra. We never want cost to be a barrier, please talk to us if you need support.
details.Camps and sleepovers: Beavers enjoy day trips and their first sleepovers as they get older. Everything is fully risk-assessed and led by trained, DBS-checked volunteers.
details.Inclusion and additional needs: Every child is welcome. Tell us about any additional needs or support that would help and we'll talk it through confidentially, there's no need to share medical detail up front.

faqs.q: What happens at the first meeting?
faqs.a: Your child is warmly welcomed and paired with existing Beavers. Expect games, meeting the leaders, and getting to know everyone. No uniform needed for the first session.
Not usually, but you're welcome to settle your child in. Leaders will let you know the drop-off and pick-up routine for your colony.

Cubs.intro: Cubs is all about fun, friends and new experiences. We help young people build confidence, learn new skills and take on bigger adventures, indoors and out.

details.Uniform: Cubs wear a green sweatshirt and a Group scarf (necker). Uniform can be bought new or second-hand, we're happy to advise on what's essential to start.
details.Costs: Subscriptions are typically £3 to 5 per week, covering weekly meetings, activities and insurance. Camps and trips cost extra. Support is available, just ask, in confidence.
details.Camps and sleepovers: Cubs enjoy indoor and outdoor camps and district events through the year, plus an annual summer camp. All camps are risk-assessed and led by qualified leaders.
details.Inclusion and additional needs: We welcome every young person. Let us know what support would help and we'll have a confidential chat, you don't need to share diagnoses or medical detail to get started.

faqs.a: Yes, Cubs can join at any time through our waiting list. When a space comes up in your local pack, we'll be in touch.
Yes! Camping is a core part of Cubs, from indoor sleepovers to outdoor and summer camps, all fully risk-assessed.

Scouts.intro: Scouts take on real expeditions, camps and challenges that build skills, teamwork and independence. It's where young people lead, problem-solve and push themselves, with plenty of adventure along the way.

details.Uniform: Scouts wear a teal Scout shirt and a Group scarf (necker). We can advise on where to buy new or second-hand and what's needed to start.
details.Costs: Subscriptions are typically £3 to 5 per week, covering weekly meetings, activities and insurance. Camps, expeditions and events cost extra. Confidential financial support is available.
details.Camps and sleepovers: Scouts camp regularly outdoors and take part in district camps, expeditions and an annual summer camp. All activities are risk-assessed and appropriately led.
details.Inclusion and additional needs: Everyone is welcome. Tell us what would help your young person take part fully and we'll talk it through confidentially.

faqs.a: Teamwork, leadership, resilience, outdoor and first-aid skills, cooking and much more, while working towards badges and awards and having fun with friends.
Safety is our top priority. All adult volunteers are DBS checked and safeguarding-trained, and every activity is risk-assessed.

Explorers.intro: Explorers is delivered through our district partnership units. Young people take on their biggest adventures yet, expeditions, Duke of Edinburgh's Award, Young Leader roles and more, with growing independence.

details.How Explorers works here: 7th Swindon has formal partnerships with Explorer units in the district, giving our Scouts a natural next step. The units are delivered in partnership rather than run directly by the Group.
details.Costs: Costs vary by unit and activity. The partnership units will explain subscriptions and any activity costs, support is available and cost should never be a barrier.
details.Young Leaders: Explorers can take on Young Leader roles, helping to run Beavers, Cubs or Scouts while developing their own leadership skills and awards.
details.Inclusion and additional needs: Explorer units welcome everyone. Let us or the unit know what support would help and it can be discussed confidentially.

faqs.q: How do Scouts move up to Explorers?
faqs.a: As young people reach around 14, we help them move on to one of our partner Explorer units. We'll support the transition and introduce the right contacts.
Both Medusa and Hydra offer great programmes. Get in touch and we'll help you find the unit that best fits, including meeting details shared privately.
